title: Killing resistant tumors with a click - Nature Biotechnology
gist: A research highlight on work by Cristina Simó and colleagues in Nature: pairing already-approved HER2 and EGFR antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates with complementary click-chemistry handles (trans-cyclooctene and tetrazine) so they crosslink inside the body, boosting antibody internalization and endolysosomal trafficking and improving antitumor activity in mouse models. The approach targets ADCs' core commercial weakness — variable antigen expression across heterogeneous tumors — using existing FDA-approved molecules rather than new biologics.

themes.theme: Antigen heterogeneity as the ADC bottleneck

insights.claim: The limiting factor on antibody-drug conjugate efficacy is not payload potency but variable target-antigen expression across heterogeneous tumors, which caps how much of a tumor any single ADC can reach.
insights.speaker: Dario Ummarino
insights.so_what: Names the mechanism behind ADC response-rate ceilings; any technology that decouples killing from uniform antigen expression expands the addressable patient pool.
insights.quote: their efficacy is hampered by the variable expression of target antigens in heterogeneous tumors

insights.claim: EGFR is singled out as a key driver of acquired tumor resistance while both HER2 and EGFR are clinically validated and expressed across many tumor types, making the HER2-EGFR pair a deliberate choice for attacking resistance rather than a convenience.
insights.speaker: Dario Ummarino
insights.so_what: Combining a validated target with a resistance driver is the design pattern to look for in next-generation ADC assets.
insights.quote: EGFR is a key driver of acquired tumor resistance

themes.theme: In-body click ligation of approved drugs

insights.claim: Simó and colleagues built antibody-ADC complexes by conjugating FDA-approved antibodies and ADCs with the complementary bioorthogonal reagents trans-cyclooctene and tetrazine, letting two approved molecules crosslink into a single multi-targeting agent.
insights.speaker: Dario Ummarino
insights.so_what: Building on already-approved molecules shortens the regulatory and manufacturing path versus engineering new bispecifics from scratch.
insights.quote: conjugated US Food and Drug Administration–approved antibodies and ADCs targeting human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) and epidermal growth factor receptor 1 (EGFR) with the complementary click reagents trans-cyclooctene and tetrazine

insights.claim: Click ligation of the antibodies increased both antibody internalization and endolysosomal trafficking in live-cell imaging of cancer cell lines, identifying uptake kinetics rather than binding affinity as the mechanism of the efficacy gain.
insights.speaker: Dario Ummarino
insights.so_what: If crosslinking drives internalization, the same trick should generalize to other ADC targets — a platform claim, not a one-asset result.
insights.quote: the antibody click ligation increased antibody internalization and endolysosomal trafficking

insights.claim: The complexes were formed by sequential dosing in mice, demonstrating that the click reaction proceeds in vivo rather than requiring pre-assembly of the complex before administration.
insights.speaker: Dario Ummarino
insights.so_what: In-body assembly changes the dosing and manufacturing model — two separately produced drugs, combined inside the patient.
insights.quote: Sequential administration of the complexes in mice demonstrated successful antibody click reactions in vivo.
